propositions: A Jira issue's KEY changes when moved between projects while its numeric id is stable, so bindings keyed on the KEY can silently detach and orphan a local ticket from a still-existing issue.
The moved_issue_key table that keeps old keys resolving can fail to update when third-party apps move issues, after which the old key stops resolving entirely.

Bindings persist the numeric jira_id alongside the key so the absence probe can retry lookup by id and re-key the binding to the issue's current key on a hit whose key differs, treating the issue as present.

The change is additive rather than re-keying the store on id, because the binding store is shared with Cloud and re-keying would rewrite the reverse index and every jira_key-taking method with large blast radius.
Bindings written before this change with no recorded jira_id continue to work unchanged with no migration, degrading to today's behavior.
The id fallback must not fire while the key still resolves, so the happy path does not double the cost of every absence probe.
